note: For maintainers: on every release, bump version (YYYY-MM-DD, then .2, .3 … for more releases that day) and add an entry at the top of releases, in words the person using EVE understands.

notes: Credit to Adam Dymitruk, whose Event Modeling method EVE follows, on the Board tab.
Look and feel and Export are tabs now (Book · Board · Look · Export), so the book is just your plan.
Export to eventmodelers.ai: the Event Book's Export button downloads your plan for EM-Studio, for working with a team or AI agents.
A Board view: your plan as a traditional event model, timeline left to right, with arrows from commands to events to views. Switch between Book and Board in the header.
After an update, the Event Book says once what's new.
The Event Book hears about a new EVE right away, not up to five minutes later.
The Event Book's header folds to one slim row while you scroll.
The Event Book's header stays at the top while you scroll.
Updates now come with release notes, here and in the Event Book.
The Event Book notices newer versions again (2026-11-01.10 was missed).
Refusals show as a red “refused” chip, like the event chips.
Refusals and failing tests are red, no longer orange like events.
The Event Book is easier to read: clearer disabled button, greyed resolved threads, shorter lines on wide screens.
Links in the Event Book use the accent colour.
The itsyBIT EVE logo in the Event Book header and as its tab icon.
The Event Book in the itsyBIT studio look.
A Look and feel card in the Event Book.
“make it beautiful” asks your design tool for three directions to pick from.
Named the ItsyBIT EVE Template.
“make it beautiful”: your plan becomes a design brief for your design tool, and the app gets the look you pick.
“update EVE”: newer tools without touching your plan or app.
Built slices fold away when you plan a new feature.
